Q6.answer: (a) Assignment rights under 351.701(b): must be held by an employee with lower standing in the same tenure group, not more than three grades (or grade intervals) below Jordan's GS-13, for which Jordan is qualified, in the same competitive area, and with the same work schedule (351.701(a)). 1. GS-12 Ellis: yes (one grade down, lower standing, full-time, same area). 2. GS-11 Frank: yes (two grades down). 3. GS-10 Gale: yes (three grades down). 4. GS-9 Hana: no (four grades down). 5. GS-12 Ito: no (higher standing). 6. GS-12 Kim: no (part-time; work schedule must match). 7. GS-12 Lund: no (different competitive area). The agency must offer the position requiring the least reduction in representative rate: Ellis's GS-12 position (351.701(a)). (b) A PE with a 30%+ compensable disability gets a five-grade limit (351.701(b)(2)). Hana's GS-9 is then within reach, and the list of positions with assignment rights becomes items 1-4. The must-offer position is still Ellis's GS-12, because it requires the least reduction in pay. (c) A Level 1 employee is not covered by 351.701(a), which applies only to a current annual rating of Level 2 or higher. Jordan has no assignment right to any of the seven positions under subpart G. (d) If Jordan and all position holders are in the excepted service, 351.701 does not apply (it applies to competitive service tenure group employees). Under 351.705(a) the agency may, at its discretion, adopt assignment provisions for excepted service employees, on the same basis as 351.701, for positions under the same appointing authority. (e) The 2026 documents do not use the words 'bumping' or 'retreating' in the regulatory text. The preamble says the new rule eliminates the multiple rounds of bumping and retreating (91 FR 49198, lines 2510-2520) and that assignment is now a comparison of performance as augmented by points. The old 351.701(d) bar on a Level 2 employee taking a position held by a higher-rated employee is eliminated (91 FR 49204, lines 3073-3078). Level 2 employees keep assignment rights as long as the lower-standing condition is met.
Q6.uncertainty: Jordan's standing would rise under a PE rule. The scenario's 'lower standing' assumptions are taken as given. Whether the agency may voluntarily offer positions outside subpart G is not addressed in the text. The meaning of 'bumping' and 'retreating' is not defined in the 2026 documents.

Q7.answer: (a) The MSPB. The notice was issued Aug 31, before Sept 2, so the OPM appeal rule does not apply (2026-15666 DATES, 91 FR 49230). The earlier rules are kept for notices issued before the effective date (2026-15665 DATES, 91 FR 49178). The Board's rule says the MSPB will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals where the agency's RIF notice was issued before Sept 2 (2026-16456, 91 FR 51997, lines 130-140). Note the inconsistency flagged in Q14(iii). (b) OPM. The notice was issued Oct 19, on or after Sept 2, so the OPM appeal rule applies (2026-15666 DATES; 351.901(a)). Appeal must be filed through OPM's electronic filing system (351.902(a), (c)). Deadline: 30 calendar days from the effective date (Dec 18, 2026). Counting: day 1 is Sat Dec 19; Dec 31 is day 13; Jan 1 is day 14; Jan 17, 2027 is day 30. Jan 17, 2027 is a Sunday, so the period extends to the first workday after it. Jan 18, 2027 is Martin Luther King Jr. Day (third Monday of January), a federal holiday, so the period runs to Tue Jan 19, 2027. Last day: Jan 19, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (351.902(b), (b)(1)). (c) Morgan must prove by a preponderance: timeliness, OPM jurisdiction, that the agency failed to comply with a statute or OPM regulation governing RIF actions under part 351, and that the failure prejudiced her by causing the action or the loss of a materially more favorable outcome (351.901(b)(1)-(4)). She is not automatically entitled to a hearing. OPM decides on the written record and holds a hearing only if it finds one 'necessary and efficient' (351.905(c)). (d) Under 351.901(c)(1)-(2), the part 351 procedures are the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action, and a RIF action or any matter relating to an appeal may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or challenged through grievance arbitration. The preamble says the final rule does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs, and that questions about the effect of particular existing agreement provisions remain for other forums (91 FR 49245, lines 1997-2005). (e) No. Under 351.901(c)(4) a party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under subpart I, and under 351.909(e) there is no further right of appeal of an OPM final decision. The preamble explains this (91 FR 49242-49243). (f) Yes. Under 351.902(b)(3), if before the appeal deadline she timely filed a complaint within the independent jurisdiction of OSC (listed in 351.901(c)(3)), and the final decision materially affects her retention standing, she may file a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the decision becomes final and is no longer subject to further administrative review. OPM decides materiality. Count: March 10, 2027 is day 0; March 31 is day 21; April 9 is day 30 (a Friday). Deadline: April 9, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. (g) The provision is in 2026-15666 (91 FR 49230), DATES paragraph: 'This final rule applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026.' The companion provision is 2026-15665 (91 FR 49178), DATES paragraph (notice before the effective date is processed under the earlier regulations).
Q7.uncertainty: (a) MSPB's rule has two inconsistent tests (see Q14(iii)); the earlier MSPB filing rules are not printed here. (f) assumes the March 10 decision is final and not subject to further administrative review, and that OPM finds materiality; the question says it would have changed her standing. The union question in (d) is unsettled by the preamble's statement on existing CBAs.

Q8.answer: (a) The current 351.806 is not reprinted in the 2026 documents. The adopted text (91 FR 65924, 2026-21320, effective Nov 18, 2026, not in force today) reads: (a) 'Under ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period'; (b) administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when the agency determines it is appropriate and consistent with 5 CFR part 630, subpart N; (c) emergency lack of work or funds (annual leave with or without consent; leave without pay with consent; nonpay without consent). The preamble says the current text uses 'when possible' in paragraph (a) (91 FR 65926). (b) Under the adopted text, employee consent is not required for administrative leave under 351.806(b). The companion provision 630.1403(c)(10) allows administrative leave for RIF-involuntarily separated employees between receipt of the notice and separation when the agency determines it is in the Government's best interests. No separate time cap appears in (c)(10). Section 630.1403(a)(3) says administrative leave is usually for no more than one workday, with longer periods permitted under the (c) circumstances or when otherwise determined appropriate by the agency. Consent is needed only for the leave-without-pay option in 351.806(c). (c) OPM says the 'Agency Policy Template' (CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025) codifies policies already in effect Governmentwide (91 FR 65928, lines 548-550) and that paragraph (b) confirms, consistent with the template, that an agency may place a RIF-affected employee on administrative leave for part or all of the notice period (91 FR 65933, lines 1103-1107). (d) No. OPM says the RIF requirements continue to apply in full and the rule does not alter RIF procedures (91 FR 65926, lines 230-234). Retention standing is fixed on receipt of the notice (351.507(a)). Notice rights are in 351.802 and 351.805, and appeal rights are in 351.901-351.902.
Q8.uncertainty: The current 351.806 text and the current 630.1403 text are not printed, so the 'before' rule is known only from preamble descriptions. The text of 630.1403(c)(10) is confirmed by its printed amendment, but no outer limit is stated for it. The Oct 26 leave is judged under the current text, which the 2026 documents describe only in part.

Q9.answer: Non-compliant: steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11 and 12. In order: steps 2, 7 and 9 (subject to the assessment and qualification standards in 351.702(a)(1)-(3), which are not reprinted). Step 1: The Aug 17 designation falls within 90 days before the Oct 13 notices (57 days). Under 351.402(c) the agency had to submit the competitive area description and a written bona fide organizational basis to OPM for approval in advance. Nothing was sent, so the designation does not comply. The designee's approval also needs checking against 351.402(b)(1) (designation cannot be delegated below the agency's headquarters level). Step 2: In order. A career-conditional employee serving an initial probationary period is excluded from competition (351.202(d)(2)(ii)); keeping her is consistent with 351.202(d)(3). Step 3: Not in order. Ortiz's supervisory probationary period does not count as an initial probationary period (definition of 'initial probationary period' in 351.203). She is a career employee not serving an initial probationary period, so she is in tenure subgroup I and must be ranked (351.502(a)(2), 351.501). Step 4: Not in order. A cutoff 30 days before Oct 13 is Sept 13. The Oct 2 rating was put on record after the cutoff and cannot be used (351.503(c)(2)). The agency must apply its cutoff uniformly within the competitive area (351.503(c)(4)); using a later rating for one employee alone is not permitted. Step 5: Not in order. Two ratings (7 and 5) require the proxy of (7+5)/2 = 6 under 351.503(f)(2). Performance credit = 6+7+5 = 18, not 15. Step 6: Not in order. Additional points for performance awards are allowed only where all employees are under a single pattern whose highest summary level is Level 3 (351.503(d)), or in multiple-pattern transmutation (351.503(e)). Here the pattern is five-level, so no added points for QSIs. Step 7: In order. Identical credit, tenure subgroup and SCD allow the agency to select any tied employee for release (351.601(c)). Step 8: Not in order. 351.602(a) prohibits releasing a competing employee while retaining in that level an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion. Reyes must not be retained in that way. Step 9: In order, subject to 351.702. Under 351.702(a)(4)(v) no assessment is required if within 5 years before the notice (Oct 13, 2021 to Oct 13, 2026) the employee occupied the same position and received a rating of Level 3 or higher in it. Silva held the position until 2023 and was rated Level 4 in 2022. Step 10: Not in order. Under 351.702(a)(4)(i)-(iii) and the 330.202 'Qualified' text, the assessment must allow demonstration of job-related skills, be based on a job analysis, and must not consist solely or principally of an automated self-assessment. Step 11: Not in order. Undue-interruption exception allows up to 90 days (351.608(b)), and the other-exceptions paragraph allows up to 90 days (351.608(g)). Exceptions may not be sequenced or stacked (351.608(a)(3)). Only one exception may be used, for no more than 90 days after Dec 14, and notice to higher-standing employees is required for exceptions over 30 days (351.608(a)(4)). Step 12: Not in order. Under 351.901(a) and 351.802(a)(6) the notice must state the right to appeal to OPM (not the MSPB), the time limit under 351.902(b), and the OPM e-filing system. The MSPB no longer hears RIF appeals for notices issued on or after Sept 2 (2026-16456).
Q9.uncertainty: Step 1: whether the designee is at headquarters level is not stated. Step 9: the qualification criteria in 351.702(a)(1)-(3) are not reprinted. The step-11 and step-4 facts are taken as stated. The final steps on order of release and the rating receipt rules depend on the agency's own written conditions under 351.503(c)(4)(i).

Q10.answer: (a) On Sept 10, 2026, paragraph (1) of the 'displaced' definition in 5 CFR 330.602 contained only its introductory text: 'A current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at grade GS-15 (or equivalent) or below (or another qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM) who:'. Paragraphs (1)(i) (RIF separation notice) and (1)(ii) (proposed removal for declining a directed geographic relocation) were absent. Amendatory instruction 11 (91 FR 49217) directed that paragraph (1) be revised and set out only the introductory text, which inadvertently removed (1)(i) and (1)(ii). (b) On Sept 15, 2026, by FR Doc. 2026-18800 (91 FR 58363, effective Sept 15, 2026), OPM restored paragraph (1) of the definition in full, with the introductory text as revised and (1)(i) and (1)(ii) as they read before the final rule. OPM acted without notice and comment under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), saying the correction restores text in effect before Sept 2 that OPM did not propose to remove and that the final rule did not discuss removing, so notice and comment are unnecessary. OPM made the correction effective on publication under 553(d)(3). It characterized the change as a non-substantive correction that 'makes no substantive change'. (c) Under the restored (1)(i), a competitive service employee who received a RIF separation notice under part 351 is displaced unless he or she has declined an offer under part 351, subpart G, of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as the position from which separated. If Nadia declines a full-time offer at a lower representative rate, the exception does not apply, and she remains displaced under (1)(i). If the offered full-time position has the same representative rate, the declined offer meets the exception and she is not displaced under (1)(i). Note that on Sept 10, for the period before the correction, (1)(i) did not exist, so she was not displaced under (1) on that day.
Q10.basis: 2026-18800 (91 FR 58363-58364), SUMMARY, Background, Need for Correction, Administrative Procedure Act paragraph and amended text of 330.602(1)(i)-(ii); 2026-15665 instruction 11 (91 FR 49217), 330.602 'displaced' (1), (2026-15665 text at p. 49217).
Q10.uncertainty: Whether any actions on Sept 2 to Sept 15 relied on the incomplete text is not addressed. The effect on RIFs noticed in that window is not stated. The text of 351.702 qualification requirements that apply to the offered position is not reprinted.

Q11.answer: Real differences found between the proposed and final regulatory text (proposed FR Doc. 2026-04377, 91 FR 10904; final 2026-15665, 91 FR 49178): (1) 351.604 (Use of furlough): proposed instruction 29 revised paragraph (b) (criteria for furlough and recall, including tenure subgroup, most recent rating, veterans' preference, length of service) and removed paragraph (d). The final rule has no instruction for 351.604 and leaves it unchanged. (2) 330.602 'displaced' paragraph (1): proposed instruction 11 revised only the introductory text of paragraph (1). The final instruction set out the whole paragraph (1) and dropped (1)(i) and (1)(ii) (corrected by 2026-18800). (3) 330.609(hh) (CTAP exception): proposed 'Retain, or finalize the appointment of, an employee serving a probationary or trial period pursuant to Civil Service Rule 11'. Final: 'serving a probationary period pursuant to Sec. 11.2 of this part' (trial period dropped; citation changed). (4) 330.707(w) (ICTAP exception): proposed revised (v) through (y) with (w) 'probationary or trial period pursuant to Civil Service Rule 11'. Final adds (w) as 'probationary period pursuant to Sec. 11.2 of this part' (trial period dropped; citation changed; a reserved paragraph before correction). (5) 351.402 (competitive area): proposed revised paragraph (b) only. Final also revises (c), so that a competitive area established or materially modified within 90 days before RIF notices must be submitted to OPM for approval in advance. (6) 351.702(a)(4)(v): final adds an exemption from assessment for an employee who within the 5 years before notice occupied the same or substantially similar position and received a Level 3 or higher rating. The proposed text does not contain this paragraph. (7) 351.802(a): proposed revised paragraphs (a)(2) and (a)(3) only. Final also adds introductory text to paragraph (a) ('Except as otherwise provided in this part, a specific written notice ... must include:'). (8) 351.805(b): proposed had no instruction for 351.805. Final revises (b) to say that an amended notice that only states a later effective date is not a new specific notice and does not require recalculation of retention standing.
Q11.uncertainty: Several part 351 and part 330 paragraphs in the proposed rule were not read line by line (for example the proposed 351.503, 351.504 and 351.203 text). Other differences may exist there. The proposed text of 351.604 is shown only through its instruction; no text of the proposed 351.604 (d) is quoted here beyond its removal.

Q12.answer: (a) Window: Oct 5, 2022 to Oct 5, 2026 (notices Oct 5, 2026). Competitive level (GS-13) register: Alvarez: PC 7+7+5 = 19; no points (B); total 19; subgroup I; SCD Apr 4, 2011. Brandt: PC 3+5+0 = 8; 5 points (AD, 30%); total 13; subgroup I; SCD Jan 9, 2014. Chen: Sept 30, 2022 rating is outside the window; two ratings in window (L5=7, L4=5); proxy (7+5)/2 = 6; PC = 6+7+5 = 18; no points (B); total 18; subgroup I; SCD May 22, 2017. Dube: career-conditional who completed probation, so tenure subgroup II (351.502(a)(3)); ratings L4 and L4 = 5+5; proxy (5+5)/2 = 5; PC 15; 3 points (A, PE without disability); total 18; SCD Aug 3, 2015. Estrada: Oct 20, 2026 rating received after notice and excluded; three most recent in window: Nov 13, 2025 (5), Nov 14, 2024 (3), Nov 15, 2023 (5) = 13; 3 points (A); total 16; subgroup I; SCD Feb 6, 2012. Farouk: one rating (L3=3) so 3x3 = 9; no points (B); total 9; subgroup I; SCD Oct 1, 2019; restoration-protected employee (see below). Quinn: excluded from competition as career-conditional in initial probation (351.202(d)(2)(ii)); not ranked. Order of retention: 1 Alvarez 19; 2 Chen 18 (subgroup I); 3 Dube 18 (subgroup II); 4 Estrada 16; 5 Brandt 13; 6 Farouk 9. (b) Released: Brandt, Estrada, Dube. Farouk was away 14 months of uniformed service (more than 180 days), so he has one year of restoration protection (353.209(b)); under 351.606(a)(1)-(2) the agency may not release him while another competing employee may be released, so he is retained despite being lowest. Brandt (13), Estrada (16) and Dube (18, subgroup II, below Chen) are the next three lowest. (c) Brandt (PE, 30%): five-grade limit, so GS-12 Gomez (17, above him), GS-11 Hill (14, above him), GS-10 Jones (15, above him) are not lower; only GS-9 Ikeda (9) is lower and within five grades. Offer: GS-9 Ikeda position. Estrada (PE, 3 points, three-grade limit): GS-12 Gomez (17) is higher; GS-11 Hill (14) and GS-10 Jones (15) are lower and within three grades; GS-9 is four grades away. Least reduction: GS-11 Hill position. Dube (PE, 3 points, three-grade limit): GS-12 Gomez (17) is lower and one grade down. Offer: GS-12 Gomez position. (d) Each released employee accepts an offer and is placed. The displaced holders (Ikeda, Hill, Gomez) then become released and may have their own assignment rights (351.701). On the facts given, Ikeda (9) has no lower-standing position within three grades below GS-9, so Ikeda would be separated. Whether the chain then separates any other holder cannot be fixed from the rules as printed.
Q12.basis: 351.501(b)-(c); 351.502(a)(2)-(3); 351.503(c)(1)-(3), (f)(2)-(3); 351.504(a)(1)-(3); 351.202(d)(2)(ii), (d)(3); 351.606(a)(1)-(2); 353.209(b) (as referenced); 351.701(a), (b)(1)-(3), (d)(2) and the five-grade PE rule in (b)(2); 351.702 (qualification for all four positions is given in the facts); preamble on career-conditional subgroup II (91 FR 49196 lines 2287-2293).
Q12.uncertainty: The chain of displacements in (d) is not fully determined by the text. Comparing retention standing across separate competitive levels (each of the four other positions is alone in its level) is not spelled out in 351.701. Farouk's protection period assumes that the 14 months were a period of uniformed service under 353.209(b). The text of 351.608 exceptions was not needed here.

Q13.answer: 1. Exception for a temporary promotion (351.602). Preamble, 91 FR 49202 (lines 2838-2842): OPM 'is also modifying Sec. 351.602 to remove the prohibition on retaining an employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment in a competitive level while releasing a competing employee from that level.' Regulatory text, 91 FR 49223 (lines 5622-5626): 'An agency may not release a competing employee from a competitive level while retaining in that level an employee with: (a) A specifically limited temporary or term promotion; or (b) A written decision under part 432 or 752 ...'. The text keeps the prohibition, and it covers temporary or term promotions, not 'appointments'. I found no other passage that states the point correctly. 2. Assessment standard (351.702(a)(4)). Preamble, 91 FR 49204 (lines 3081-3086): the assessment 'does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination'. Regulatory text, 91 FR 49226 (lines 5992-5993): 'Does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment.' The preamble's standard ('does not rely on') is broader than the text ('solely of, or principally rely on'). The Executive Summary (91 FR 49178) gives the same description as the text.
Q13.uncertainty: I checked the main preamble only in targeted passages (cutoff, ratings window, 351.608, 351.701, 351.705, 351.805, 351.606, and the Executive Summary). Other mismatches may exist in parts of the preamble I did not read in full, such as the section-by-section discussion of 351.202 and 351.503(d).

Q14.answer: (i) Preamble vs text: (a) Appeals preamble (91 FR 49249, lines 2496-2498) says an appeal may be filed within 30 days 'after the final decision on that matter'. Regulatory text 351.902(b)(3) (91 FR 49264, lines 4329-4331) says 30 days 'after the date on which the decision ... becomes final and is no longer subject to further administrative review.' The preamble's summary (91 FR 49231, lines 179-180) includes the 'no longer subject to further administrative review' condition, so another passage states it correctly. I found no other mismatch between the appeals preamble and the regulatory text in the passages checked. (ii) Changes from the proposed rule not acknowledged in the final rule's summary of changes (91 FR 49230-49232): (a) Proposed 351.901(c) said the part 351 procedures 'shall supersede any appeal procedures found in agency policies or collective bargaining agreements' (proposed text, 2026-02576, 91 FR 5875, lines 1922-1925). The final 351.901(c) (91 FR 49263, lines 4279-4281) drops that sentence. The summary does not mention this. (b) Proposed 351.901(c) listed the Federal Labor Relations Authority among bodies that could still receive a complaint (91 FR 5875, lines 1926-1929). Final 351.901(c)(3) (91 FR 49264, lines 4291-4295) omits the FLRA. The summary's list (91 FR 49230, lines 156-158) omits it too. (c) Proposed 351.903(b) required the agency response 'within 30 calendar days of the initial appeal' (91 FR 5876, lines 2018-2019). Final 351.903(b)(1) says 'within 30 calendar days after service of the initial appeal' (91 FR 49264, lines 4390-4391). The summary does not mention this. (iii) Inconsistencies about which RIF appeals the Board will hear: (a) Within the Board's rule, 91 FR 51997 (lines 130-140) says the MSPB will accept and adjudicate RIF appeals where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the effective date. Section III, 91 FR 51998 (lines 182-184), instead keys on whether 'the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026'. The two tests differ: for a notice issued Aug 31 with an Oct 30 effective date, section II points to the MSPB, while section III does not apply. (b) OPM's rule applies only to RIF notices issued on or after Sept 2 (91 FR 49230, DATES). So for such a notice, neither the OPM rule nor the section III test clearly covers it. (c) The Board's Dates paragraph uses 'agency actions taken before the effective date' (91 FR 51997), a third trigger that does not match OPM's notice-date trigger.
Q14.uncertainty: The list is limited to items I checked against text. I did not read the full proposed rule text for 351.903-351.909, so further differences may exist there. The Board's rule may have additional statements about Foreign Service RIF appeals under 22 U.S.C. 4010a that conflict with OPM's 'may appeal to OPM' language; I did not verify that conflict in the text.

Q2.answer: (a) Performance credit (PC) per 351.503(a)(1): Level 5=7, Level 4=5, Level 3=3, Level 2 or 1=0. Veterans' points per 351.504(a): 30%+ PE=5 (Subgroup AD); other PE=3 (Subgroup A); non-PE=0 (Subgroup B). Abbott: PC 7+5+5=17; 0 points (B); total 17. Bianchi: PC 5+0+3=8; 5 points (AD); total 13. Castillo: not a preference eligible under 351.504(b) (see Q3); PC 7+5+5=17; 0 points (B); total 17. Dalton: two ratings only, so 351.503(f)(2) proxy = (7+0)/2 = 3.5; PC = 3.5+7+0 = 10.5; 3 points (A); total 13.5. Eze: PC 5+5+5=15; 0 points (B); total 15. Fontaine: one rating only, so 351.503(f)(3): 5x3 = 15; 0 points (B); total 15. (b) Order of retention (351.501): Abbott 17 (career, subgroup I, SCD May 1, 2003) and Castillo 17 (subgroup I, SCD Aug 1, 2012) tie on 17; tie broken by tenure subgroup (both I) then earliest SCD, so Abbott ranks above Castillo. Fontaine 15 (subgroup I) and Eze 15 (competitive subgroup II, 351.502(a)(3)) tie; subgroup I ranks ahead, so Fontaine ranks above Eze. Then Dalton 13.5, then Bianchi 13. Order: 1 Abbott, 2 Castillo, 3 Fontaine, 4 Eze, 5 Dalton, 6 Bianchi. Released: Bianchi and Dalton (the two lowest). (c) Under the earlier rules Bianchi would stand above Abbott. The earlier rules ranked employees first by tenure group, then by veterans' preference subgroup AD, A, B, and only then by performance-adjusted service dates. Bianchi (AD) therefore outranks Abbott (B) regardless of ratings. (d) Under 351.506(c)(1) Bianchi may review the complete retention register, including the names of all others on it, the performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference, and the SCDs used to establish the competitive level and standings; she may also review related registers under 351.506(c)(2) and inspect under 351.506(b)(1), subject to FOIA and Privacy Act limits under 351.506(e).
Q2.uncertainty: Eze's tenure group depends on whether a four-year term appointment is competitive or excepted service; the scenario says the employee is in the same competitive level, so subgroup II competitive service is assumed. The release order rule (351.601(a)-(b)) is not reprinted in the 2026 text; lowest standing released first is assumed. Retention standing across the registers and how an SCD is verified are not addressed. Castillo's and Dalton's ratings are assumed to fall within the four-year window.

Q3.answer: (a) A: not a preference eligible; 0 points; subgroup B. Deciding paragraph 351.504(b): (b)(1) not met (retirement not disability-based); (b)(2) not met because retired pay is based on 22 years (20 or more); (b)(3) not met. B: not a preference eligible; 0 points; subgroup B. Under 351.504(b) the 40% disability does not help. (b)(1) not met; (b)(2) not met (21 years); (b)(3) not met. C: preference eligible; 5 points; subgroup AD. Under 351.504(b)(1)(i) the disability resulted from injury in the line of duty as a direct result of armed conflict. (b)(4) is satisfied because C is a disabled veteran (60%). D: not a preference eligible; 0 points; subgroup B. (b)(2) not met (24 years). E: preference eligible; 3 points; subgroup A. (b)(1) not met, but (b)(2) is met because retired pay is not based on 20 or more years (16 years). Disability is 10%, below 30%, so 351.504(a)(2) gives 3 points. (b) A: retired member not a PE, so 351.505(b)(2)(i) credits only campaign service (2 years). SCD = Sept 7, 2010 minus 2 years = Sept 7, 2008 (351.505(d)(2)). C: PE, so 351.505(b)(2)(ii) credits total active service (14 years). SCD = Sept 7, 2010 minus 14 years = Sept 7, 1996. (c) Under the amended rules the subgroups AD, A and B are identifiers on the register, not ranking tiers. Points augment performance credit (351.504(a)); the order of retention ranks employees by performance credit as augmented by points (351.501(b)); ties are broken by tenure subgroup I/II and then SCD (351.501(c)). The subgroups do not decide the order themselves. Under the earlier rules the AD/A/B subgroups were the ranking tier, applied before performance (91 FR 49198).
Q3.uncertainty: For E, the regulation does not say whether a medical retirement with disability-based pay is 'not based upon 20 or more years'; the text reads the test as years of service, so E is treated as a PE. The scenario's 'continuously employed since 1964' is treated as not met.

Q4.answer: (a) Notices Sept 3, 2026; four-year window runs from Sept 3, 2022. Three most recent ratings: Aug 10, 2026 (L5=7), Nov 14, 2025 (L3=3), Nov 15, 2024 (L3=3). Performance credit = 13. (b) Cutoff = 45 days before Sept 3, 2026 = July 20, 2026 (Sept 3 back 3 days to Aug 31, 31 more to July 31, 11 more to July 20). Window for the cutoff: July 20, 2022 to July 20, 2026. The Aug 10, 2026 rating is after the cutoff and cannot be used. Three most recent in window: Nov 14, 2025 (3), Nov 15, 2024 (3), Nov 20, 2023 (5). Performance credit = 11. (c) No. The rating was given to the employee on July 15 but was not put on record until Aug 15, after the July 20 cutoff. A rating must be on record (available to the office building the registers) to be considered (351.503(c)(3)), and no new ratings put on record after the cutoff may be used (351.503(c)(2)). The agency's definition of when a rating is 'received' (351.503(c)(4)(i)) governs window placement, but it does not cure the later on-record date. (d) Window from Sept 3, 2022. The Aug 15, 2022 rating is outside the window. Two ratings remain: Nov 15, 2024 (L4=5) and Nov 14, 2025 (L3=3). Proxy = (5+3)/2 = 4 (351.503(f)(2)). Performance credit = 4+5+3 = 12. (e) No rating of record in four years, so 351.503(f)(1) applies: performance credit is based on the modal rating for the summary-level pattern of his position of record. The most defensible reading is three times the points for that modal rating, as in (f)(3). If the modal rating is Level 3, the result is 9. The modal-rating definition in 351.203 is not reprinted in the 2026 text, so the exact modal value cannot be confirmed from the Federal Register. Outside ratings count only if the agency determines they are equivalent to ratings of record (351.503(b)(3)).
Q4.uncertainty: The modal-rating definition and the rule for valuing zero ratings are not in the printed text; (e) therefore depends on the pre-existing definition in 351.203, which is not printed in the 2026 documents. The 'received' date conditions are left to each agency under 351.503(c)(4).

Q5.answer: (a) Earlier rules (notices before Sept 2): Lee is retained and Park is released. Under the earlier rules, tenure group I and subgroup B are the same for both. Adjusted SCD = actual SCD minus additional years from ratings (Level 3 = 12 years, Level 4 = 16, Level 5 = 20). Lee: SCD Mar 2, 1998 minus 12 (3/3/3) = Mar 2, 1986. Park: SCD July 8, 2019 minus 20 (5/5/5) = July 8, 1999. The earlier adjusted SCD ranks higher, so Lee (1986) ranks above Park (1999) and Park is released. New rules (notices Sept 2 or Sept 3): PC Lee 3+3+3=9; Park 7+7+7=21. Park ranks above Lee, so Lee is released in both (ii) and (iii). (b) No. The Nov 2 date moved to Nov 30 by amended notice does not require a new notice or recalculation: 351.805(b) says an amended notice solely stating a later effective date is not a new specific RIF notice and does not require recalculation of retention standing. Retention standing is fixed as of receipt of the specific notice (351.507(a)), and the Oct 15 rating is outside the four-year period prior to the Sept 3 notices (351.503(c)(1)). (c) (1) Which version applies: the date the agency issues the specific RIF notice (2026-15665 DATES: a notice issued before Sept 2, 2026 is processed under the rules in effect when issued). (2) The end of the four-year rating period: the date of issuance of RIF notices (351.503(c)(1)), or the agency's cutoff date if one is set (351.503(c)(2)). (3) Tenure subgroup and retention standing: the date the employee receives a specific RIF notice (351.502(a)(2) and (b)(2); 351.507(a)).
Q5.basis: 351.503(a)(1), (c)(1)-(2); 351.505(d); 351.502(a)(2); 351.507(a); 351.805(b) (91 FR 49178, pp. 49219-49226). Earlier rules: 91 FR 49186 lines 1090-1094 (Level 5 adds 20 years, Level 4 16, Level 3 12) and 91 FR 49198 lines 2496-2503 (tenure, then veterans' preference subgroup, then adjusted SCD).
Q5.uncertainty: The earlier-rule result rests on the preamble's description (adjusted SCD with Level 3=12 years, Level 5=20 years); the earlier 5 CFR 351.504 text is not printed in the 2026 documents, so it is not checked directly. The Aug 28 notice is also unconfirmed for the effective-date rule's application to a notice issued before Sept 2.

Q6.answer: (a) Assignment rights under 351.701(b): must be held by an employee with lower standing in the same tenure group, not more than three grades (or grade intervals) below Jordan's GS-13, for which Jordan is qualified, in the same competitive area, and with the same work schedule (351.701(a)). 1. GS-12 Ellis: yes (one grade down, lower standing, full-time, same area). 2. GS-11 Frank: yes (two grades down). 3. GS-10 Gale: yes (three grades down). 4. GS-9 Hana: no (four grades down). 5. GS-12 Ito: no (higher standing). 6. GS-12 Kim: no (part-time; work schedule must match). 7. GS-12 Lund: no (different competitive area). The agency must offer the position requiring the least reduction in representative rate: Ellis's GS-12 position (351.701(a)). (b) A PE with a 30%+ compensable disability gets a five-grade limit (351.701(b)(2)). Hana's GS-9 is then within reach, and the list of positions with assignment rights becomes items 1-4. The must-offer position is still Ellis's GS-12, because it requires the least reduction in pay. (c) A Level 1 employee is not covered by 351.701(a), which applies only to a current annual rating of Level 2 or higher. Jordan has no assignment right to any of the seven positions under subpart G. (d) If Jordan and all position holders are in the excepted service, 351.701 does not apply (it applies to competitive service tenure group employees). Under 351.705(a) the agency may, at its discretion, adopt assignment provisions for excepted service employees, on the same basis as 351.701, for positions under the same appointing authority. (e) The 2026 documents do not use the words 'bumping' or 'retreating' in the regulatory text. The preamble says the new rule eliminates the multiple rounds of bumping and retreating (91 FR 49198, lines 2510-2520) and that assignment is now a comparison of performance as augmented by points. The old 351.701(d) bar on a Level 2 employee taking a position held by a higher-rated employee is eliminated (91 FR 49204, lines 3073-3078). Level 2 employees keep assignment rights as long as the lower-standing condition is met.
Q6.uncertainty: Jordan's standing would rise under a PE rule. The scenario's 'lower standing' assumptions are taken as given. Whether the agency may voluntarily offer positions outside subpart G is not addressed in the text. The meaning of 'bumping' and 'retreating' is not defined in the 2026 documents.

Q7.answer: (a) The MSPB. The notice was issued Aug 31, before Sept 2, so the OPM appeal rule does not apply (2026-15666 DATES, 91 FR 49230). The earlier rules are kept for notices issued before the effective date (2026-15665 DATES, 91 FR 49178). The Board's rule says the MSPB will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals where the agency's RIF notice was issued before Sept 2 (2026-16456, 91 FR 51997, lines 130-140). Note the inconsistency flagged in Q14(iii). (b) OPM. The notice was issued Oct 19, on or after Sept 2, so the OPM appeal rule applies (2026-15666 DATES; 351.901(a)). Appeal must be filed through OPM's electronic filing system (351.902(a), (c)). Deadline: 30 calendar days from the effective date (Dec 18, 2026). Counting: day 1 is Sat Dec 19; Dec 31 is day 13; Jan 1 is day 14; Jan 17, 2027 is day 30. Jan 17, 2027 is a Sunday, so the period extends to the first workday after it. Jan 18, 2027 is Martin Luther King Jr. Day (third Monday of January), a federal holiday, so the period runs to Tue Jan 19, 2027. Last day: Jan 19, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (351.902(b), (b)(1)). (c) Morgan must prove by a preponderance: timeliness, OPM jurisdiction, that the agency failed to comply with a statute or OPM regulation governing RIF actions under part 351, and that the failure prejudiced her by causing the action or the loss of a materially more favorable outcome (351.901(b)(1)-(4)). She is not automatically entitled to a hearing. OPM decides on the written record and holds a hearing only if it finds one 'necessary and efficient' (351.905(c)). (d) Under 351.901(c)(1)-(2), the part 351 procedures are the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action, and a RIF action or any matter relating to an appeal may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or challenged through grievance arbitration. The preamble says the final rule does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs, and that questions about the effect of particular existing agreement provisions remain for other forums (91 FR 49245, lines 1997-2005). (e) No. Under 351.901(c)(4) a party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under subpart I, and under 351.909(e) there is no further right of appeal of an OPM final decision. The preamble explains this (91 FR 49242-49243). (f) Yes. Under 351.902(b)(3), if before the appeal deadline she timely filed a complaint within the independent jurisdiction of OSC (listed in 351.901(c)(3)), and the final decision materially affects her retention standing, she may file a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the decision becomes final and is no longer subject to further administrative review. OPM decides materiality. Count: March 10, 2027 is day 0; March 31 is day 21; April 9 is day 30 (a Friday). Deadline: April 9, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. (g) The provision is in 2026-15666 (91 FR 49230), DATES paragraph: 'This final rule applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026.' The companion provision is 2026-15665 (91 FR 49178), DATES paragraph (notice before the effective date is processed under the earlier regulations).
Q7.uncertainty: (a) MSPB's rule has two inconsistent tests (see Q14(iii)); the earlier MSPB filing rules are not printed here. (f) assumes the March 10 decision is final and not subject to further administrative review, and that OPM finds materiality; the question says it would have changed her standing. The union question in (d) is unsettled by the preamble's statement on existing CBAs.

Q8.answer: (a) The current 351.806 is not reprinted in the 2026 documents. The adopted text (91 FR 65924, 2026-21320, effective Nov 18, 2026, not in force today) reads: (a) 'Under ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period'; (b) administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when the agency determines it is appropriate and consistent with 5 CFR part 630, subpart N; (c) emergency lack of work or funds (annual leave with or without consent; leave without pay with consent; nonpay without consent). The preamble says the current text uses 'when possible' in paragraph (a) (91 FR 65926). (b) Under the adopted text, employee consent is not required for administrative leave under 351.806(b). The companion provision 630.1403(c)(10) allows administrative leave for RIF-involuntarily separated employees between receipt of the notice and separation when the agency determines it is in the Government's best interests. No separate time cap appears in (c)(10). Section 630.1403(a)(3) says administrative leave is usually for no more than one workday, with longer periods permitted under the (c) circumstances or when otherwise determined appropriate by the agency. Consent is needed only for the leave-without-pay option in 351.806(c). (c) OPM says the 'Agency Policy Template' (CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025) codifies policies already in effect Governmentwide (91 FR 65928, lines 548-550) and that paragraph (b) confirms, consistent with the template, that an agency may place a RIF-affected employee on administrative leave for part or all of the notice period (91 FR 65933, lines 1103-1107). (d) No. OPM says the RIF requirements continue to apply in full and the rule does not alter RIF procedures (91 FR 65926, lines 230-234). Retention standing is fixed on receipt of the notice (351.507(a)). Notice rights are in 351.802 and 351.805, and appeal rights are in 351.901-351.902.
Q8.uncertainty: The current 351.806 text and the current 630.1403 text are not printed, so the 'before' rule is known only from preamble descriptions. The text of 630.1403(c)(10) is confirmed by its printed amendment, but no outer limit is stated for it. The Oct 26 leave is judged under the current text, which the 2026 documents describe only in part.

Q9.answer: Non-compliant: steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11 and 12. In order: steps 2, 7 and 9 (subject to the assessment and qualification standards in 351.702(a)(1)-(3), which are not reprinted). Step 1: The Aug 17 designation falls within 90 days before the Oct 13 notices (57 days). Under 351.402(c) the agency had to submit the competitive area description and a written bona fide organizational basis to OPM for approval in advance. Nothing was sent, so the designation does not comply. The designee's approval also needs checking against 351.402(b)(1) (designation cannot be delegated below the agency's headquarters level). Step 2: In order. A career-conditional employee serving an initial probationary period is excluded from competition (351.202(d)(2)(ii)); keeping her is consistent with 351.202(d)(3). Step 3: Not in order. Ortiz's supervisory probationary period does not count as an initial probationary period (definition of 'initial probationary period' in 351.203). She is a career employee not serving an initial probationary period, so she is in tenure subgroup I and must be ranked (351.502(a)(2), 351.501). Step 4: Not in order. A cutoff 30 days before Oct 13 is Sept 13. The Oct 2 rating was put on record after the cutoff and cannot be used (351.503(c)(2)). The agency must apply its cutoff uniformly within the competitive area (351.503(c)(4)); using a later rating for one employee alone is not permitted. Step 5: Not in order. Two ratings (7 and 5) require the proxy of (7+5)/2 = 6 under 351.503(f)(2). Performance credit = 6+7+5 = 18, not 15. Step 6: Not in order. Additional points for performance awards are allowed only where all employees are under a single pattern whose highest summary level is Level 3 (351.503(d)), or in multiple-pattern transmutation (351.503(e)). Here the pattern is five-level, so no added points for QSIs. Step 7: In order. Identical credit, tenure subgroup and SCD allow the agency to select any tied employee for release (351.601(c)). Step 8: Not in order. 351.602(a) prohibits releasing a competing employee while retaining in that level an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion. Reyes must not be retained in that way. Step 9: In order, subject to 351.702. Under 351.702(a)(4)(v) no assessment is required if within 5 years before the notice (Oct 13, 2021 to Oct 13, 2026) the employee occupied the same position and received a rating of Level 3 or higher in it. Silva held the position until 2023 and was rated Level 4 in 2022. Step 10: Not in order. Under 351.702(a)(4)(i)-(iii) and the 330.202 'Qualified' text, the assessment must allow demonstration of job-related skills, be based on a job analysis, and must not consist solely or principally of an automated self-assessment. Step 11: Not in order. Undue-interruption exception allows up to 90 days (351.608(b)), and the other-exceptions paragraph allows up to 90 days (351.608(g)). Exceptions may not be sequenced or stacked (351.608(a)(3)). Only one exception may be used, for no more than 90 days after Dec 14, and notice to higher-standing employees is required for exceptions over 30 days (351.608(a)(4)). Step 12: Not in order. Under 351.901(a) and 351.802(a)(6) the notice must state the right to appeal to OPM (not the MSPB), the time limit under 351.902(b), and the OPM e-filing system. The MSPB no longer hears RIF appeals for notices issued on or after Sept 2 (2026-16456).
Q9.uncertainty: Step 1: whether the designee is at headquarters level is not stated. Step 9: the qualification criteria in 351.702(a)(1)-(3) are not reprinted. The step-11 and step-4 facts are taken as stated. The final steps on order of release and the rating receipt rules depend on the agency's own written conditions under 351.503(c)(4)(i).

Q10.answer: (a) On Sept 10, 2026, paragraph (1) of the 'displaced' definition in 5 CFR 330.602 contained only its introductory text: 'A current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at grade GS-15 (or equivalent) or below (or another qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM) who:'. Paragraphs (1)(i) (RIF separation notice) and (1)(ii) (proposed removal for declining a directed geographic relocation) were absent. Amendatory instruction 11 (91 FR 49217) directed that paragraph (1) be revised and set out only the introductory text, which inadvertently removed (1)(i) and (1)(ii). (b) On Sept 15, 2026, by FR Doc. 2026-18800 (91 FR 58363, effective Sept 15, 2026), OPM restored paragraph (1) of the definition in full, with the introductory text as revised and (1)(i) and (1)(ii) as they read before the final rule. OPM acted without notice and comment under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), saying the correction restores text in effect before Sept 2 that OPM did not propose to remove and that the final rule did not discuss removing, so notice and comment are unnecessary. OPM made the correction effective on publication under 553(d)(3). It characterized the change as a non-substantive correction that 'makes no substantive change'. (c) Under the restored (1)(i), a competitive service employee who received a RIF separation notice under part 351 is displaced unless he or she has declined an offer under part 351, subpart G, of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as the position from which separated. If Nadia declines a full-time offer at a lower representative rate, the exception does not apply, and she remains displaced under (1)(i). If the offered full-time position has the same representative rate, the declined offer meets the exception and she is not displaced under (1)(i). Note that on Sept 10, for the period before the correction, (1)(i) did not exist, so she was not displaced under (1) on that day.
Q10.basis: 2026-18800 (91 FR 58363-58364), SUMMARY, Background, Need for Correction, Administrative Procedure Act paragraph and amended text of 330.602(1)(i)-(ii); 2026-15665 instruction 11 (91 FR 49217), 330.602 'displaced' (1), (2026-15665 text at p. 49217).
Q10.uncertainty: Whether any actions on Sept 2 to Sept 15 relied on the incomplete text is not addressed. The effect on RIFs noticed in that window is not stated. The text of 351.702 qualification requirements that apply to the offered position is not reprinted.

Q11.answer: Real differences found between the proposed and final regulatory text (proposed FR Doc. 2026-04377, 91 FR 10904; final 2026-15665, 91 FR 49178): (1) 351.604 (Use of furlough): proposed instruction 29 revised paragraph (b) (criteria for furlough and recall, including tenure subgroup, most recent rating, veterans' preference, length of service) and removed paragraph (d). The final rule has no instruction for 351.604 and leaves it unchanged. (2) 330.602 'displaced' paragraph (1): proposed instruction 11 revised only the introductory text of paragraph (1). The final instruction set out the whole paragraph (1) and dropped (1)(i) and (1)(ii) (corrected by 2026-18800). (3) 330.609(hh) (CTAP exception): proposed 'Retain, or finalize the appointment of, an employee serving a probationary or trial period pursuant to Civil Service Rule 11'. Final: 'serving a probationary period pursuant to Sec. 11.2 of this part' (trial period dropped; citation changed). (4) 330.707(w) (ICTAP exception): proposed revised (v) through (y) with (w) 'probationary or trial period pursuant to Civil Service Rule 11'. Final adds (w) as 'probationary period pursuant to Sec. 11.2 of this part' (trial period dropped; citation changed; a reserved paragraph before correction). (5) 351.402 (competitive area): proposed revised paragraph (b) only. Final also revises (c), so that a competitive area established or materially modified within 90 days before RIF notices must be submitted to OPM for approval in advance. (6) 351.702(a)(4)(v): final adds an exemption from assessment for an employee who within the 5 years before notice occupied the same or substantially similar position and received a Level 3 or higher rating. The proposed text does not contain this paragraph. (7) 351.802(a): proposed revised paragraphs (a)(2) and (a)(3) only. Final also adds introductory text to paragraph (a) ('Except as otherwise provided in this part, a specific written notice ... must include:'). (8) 351.805(b): proposed had no instruction for 351.805. Final revises (b) to say that an amended notice that only states a later effective date is not a new specific notice and does not require recalculation of retention standing.
Q11.uncertainty: Several part 351 and part 330 paragraphs in the proposed rule were not read line by line (for example the proposed 351.503, 351.504 and 351.203 text). Other differences may exist there. The proposed text of 351.604 is shown only through its instruction; no text of the proposed 351.604 (d) is quoted here beyond its removal.

Q12.answer: (a) Window: Oct 5, 2022 to Oct 5, 2026 (notices Oct 5, 2026). Competitive level (GS-13) register: Alvarez: PC 7+7+5 = 19; no points (B); total 19; subgroup I; SCD Apr 4, 2011. Brandt: PC 3+5+0 = 8; 5 points (AD, 30%); total 13; subgroup I; SCD Jan 9, 2014. Chen: Sept 30, 2022 rating is outside the window; two ratings in window (L5=7, L4=5); proxy (7+5)/2 = 6; PC = 6+7+5 = 18; no points (B); total 18; subgroup I; SCD May 22, 2017. Dube: career-conditional who completed probation, so tenure subgroup II (351.502(a)(3)); ratings L4 and L4 = 5+5; proxy (5+5)/2 = 5; PC 15; 3 points (A, PE without disability); total 18; SCD Aug 3, 2015. Estrada: Oct 20, 2026 rating received after notice and excluded; three most recent in window: Nov 13, 2025 (5), Nov 14, 2024 (3), Nov 15, 2023 (5) = 13; 3 points (A); total 16; subgroup I; SCD Feb 6, 2012. Farouk: one rating (L3=3) so 3x3 = 9; no points (B); total 9; subgroup I; SCD Oct 1, 2019; restoration-protected employee (see below). Quinn: excluded from competition as career-conditional in initial probation (351.202(d)(2)(ii)); not ranked. Order of retention: 1 Alvarez 19; 2 Chen 18 (subgroup I); 3 Dube 18 (subgroup II); 4 Estrada 16; 5 Brandt 13; 6 Farouk 9. (b) Released: Brandt, Estrada, Dube. Farouk was away 14 months of uniformed service (more than 180 days), so he has one year of restoration protection (353.209(b)); under 351.606(a)(1)-(2) the agency may not release him while another competing employee may be released, so he is retained despite being lowest. Brandt (13), Estrada (16) and Dube (18, subgroup II, below Chen) are the next three lowest. (c) Brandt (PE, 30%): five-grade limit, so GS-12 Gomez (17, above him), GS-11 Hill (14, above him), GS-10 Jones (15, above him) are not lower; only GS-9 Ikeda (9) is lower and within five grades. Offer: GS-9 Ikeda position. Estrada (PE, 3 points, three-grade limit): GS-12 Gomez (17) is higher; GS-11 Hill (14) and GS-10 Jones (15) are lower and within three grades; GS-9 is four grades away. Least reduction: GS-11 Hill position. Dube (PE, 3 points, three-grade limit): GS-12 Gomez (17) is lower and one grade down. Offer: GS-12 Gomez position. (d) Each released employee accepts an offer and is placed. The displaced holders (Ikeda, Hill, Gomez) then become released and may have their own assignment rights (351.701). On the facts given, Ikeda (9) has no lower-standing position within three grades below GS-9, so Ikeda would be separated. Whether the chain then separates any other holder cannot be fixed from the rules as printed.
Q12.basis: 351.501(b)-(c); 351.502(a)(2)-(3); 351.503(c)(1)-(3), (f)(2)-(3); 351.504(a)(1)-(3); 351.202(d)(2)(ii), (d)(3); 351.606(a)(1)-(2); 353.209(b) (as referenced); 351.701(a), (b)(1)-(3), (d)(2) and the five-grade PE rule in (b)(2); 351.702 (qualification for all four positions is given in the facts); preamble on career-conditional subgroup II (91 FR 49196 lines 2287-2293).
Q12.uncertainty: The chain of displacements in (d) is not fully determined by the text. Comparing retention standing across separate competitive levels (each of the four other positions is alone in its level) is not spelled out in 351.701. Farouk's protection period assumes that the 14 months were a period of uniformed service under 353.209(b). The text of 351.608 exceptions was not needed here.

Q13.answer: 1. Exception for a temporary promotion (351.602). Preamble, 91 FR 49202 (lines 2838-2842): OPM 'is also modifying Sec. 351.602 to remove the prohibition on retaining an employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment in a competitive level while releasing a competing employee from that level.' Regulatory text, 91 FR 49223 (lines 5622-5626): 'An agency may not release a competing employee from a competitive level while retaining in that level an employee with: (a) A specifically limited temporary or term promotion; or (b) A written decision under part 432 or 752 ...'. The text keeps the prohibition, and it covers temporary or term promotions, not 'appointments'. I found no other passage that states the point correctly. 2. Assessment standard (351.702(a)(4)). Preamble, 91 FR 49204 (lines 3081-3086): the assessment 'does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination'. Regulatory text, 91 FR 49226 (lines 5992-5993): 'Does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment.' The preamble's standard ('does not rely on') is broader than the text ('solely of, or principally rely on'). The Executive Summary (91 FR 49178) gives the same description as the text.
Q13.uncertainty: I checked the main preamble only in targeted passages (cutoff, ratings window, 351.608, 351.701, 351.705, 351.805, 351.606, and the Executive Summary). Other mismatches may exist in parts of the preamble I did not read in full, such as the section-by-section discussion of 351.202 and 351.503(d).

Q14.answer: (i) Preamble vs text: (a) Appeals preamble (91 FR 49249, lines 2496-2498) says an appeal may be filed within 30 days 'after the final decision on that matter'. Regulatory text 351.902(b)(3) (91 FR 49264, lines 4329-4331) says 30 days 'after the date on which the decision ... becomes final and is no longer subject to further administrative review.' The preamble's summary (91 FR 49231, lines 179-180) includes the 'no longer subject to further administrative review' condition, so another passage states it correctly. I found no other mismatch between the appeals preamble and the regulatory text in the passages checked. (ii) Changes from the proposed rule not acknowledged in the final rule's summary of changes (91 FR 49230-49232): (a) Proposed 351.901(c) said the part 351 procedures 'shall supersede any appeal procedures found in agency policies or collective bargaining agreements' (proposed text, 2026-02576, 91 FR 5875, lines 1922-1925). The final 351.901(c) (91 FR 49263, lines 4279-4281) drops that sentence. The summary does not mention this. (b) Proposed 351.901(c) listed the Federal Labor Relations Authority among bodies that could still receive a complaint (91 FR 5875, lines 1926-1929). Final 351.901(c)(3) (91 FR 49264, lines 4291-4295) omits the FLRA. The summary's list (91 FR 49230, lines 156-158) omits it too. (c) Proposed 351.903(b) required the agency response 'within 30 calendar days of the initial appeal' (91 FR 5876, lines 2018-2019). Final 351.903(b)(1) says 'within 30 calendar days after service of the initial appeal' (91 FR 49264, lines 4390-4391). The summary does not mention this. (iii) Inconsistencies about which RIF appeals the Board will hear: (a) Within the Board's rule, 91 FR 51997 (lines 130-140) says the MSPB will accept and adjudicate RIF appeals where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the effective date. Section III, 91 FR 51998 (lines 182-184), instead keys on whether 'the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026'. The two tests differ: for a notice issued Aug 31 with an Oct 30 effective date, section II points to the MSPB, while section III does not apply. (b) OPM's rule applies only to RIF notices issued on or after Sept 2 (91 FR 49230, DATES). So for such a notice, neither the OPM rule nor the section III test clearly covers it. (c) The Board's Dates paragraph uses 'agency actions taken before the effective date' (91 FR 51997), a third trigger that does not match OPM's notice-date trigger.
Q14.uncertainty: The list is limited to items I checked against text. I did not read the full proposed rule text for 351.903-351.909, so further differences may exist there. The Board's rule may have additional statements about Foreign Service RIF appeals under 22 U.S.C. 4010a that conflict with OPM's 'may appeal to OPM' language; I did not verify that conflict in the text.
